title: I have never felt so at peace with myself - an autumnal evening 2021
en: it was a quiet evening at the cottage yesterday the days are quickly growing darker and already several of my more delicate flowers have been taken by an early morning frost i try to spend at least half an hour reading every night and lately the days have been so much shorter i've embraced lighting candles i remember as a literature student in ireland i read about how people used tallow candles in the past they were made of animal fat and smelled horrible consequently paraffin and other types of wax were much preferred and eventually replaced it i'm quite grateful i can let my beeswax tapers and that my home smells like

roasted honey instead of animal fat i find that using softer lights this time of year helped connect me to the season bringing more of an awareness on how things are changing how it is affecting the plants and animals it is a harbinger of the coldest half of the year a warning to the natural world to prepare and haste as time is running out

over here the cottonwoods are some of the first to shed their leaves i think of them as having quite cautious personalities much like my own the moment things seem overly dry or at the slightest hint of a frost they begin to diminish drop their leaves and grow dormant the other trees soon follow suit and the little animals busily prepare their food stores i've said goodbye to many birds in this area gone to warmer climates until the spring for once i'm not jealous of them since after a hot rainless summer i am welcoming the cold so is my dog who loves being outdoors this time of year as he does not get overheated
so in the spirit of the changing seasons i

thought i'd create some new decorations for my home recently i've been reading a lot about old photography techniques from the past my interest was peaked since i spent so much more time using my camera this year the technique of making blueprints also known as cianotypes is one that originated over a hundred years ago after its invention a woman named anna adkins became known for using the technique in making shadowgraphs of algae the process has a fascinating history and was still in use in some lines of work up until modern printers became popular nowadays the technique is preserved by artists and photographers interested in the niche and their professional ciano types are no doubt much better than my own amateur attempts however it is so much fun to try new things and through

that relive more positive aspects of the past now and then i get comments on my videos comparing how we live today to those in the past often romanticizing an era before technology and industrialization took over while there definitely has been a lot lost through these transitions and many tragedies in the process i believe much has also been gained depending on how you look at it as someone who loves history and learning about the past through my own process of discovery i began to deeply value living not only in my specific

location but in this century for example my mother is not white and she and my father would have struggled to have their marriage legally recognized in the u.s up until the 60s my existence wouldn't be guaranteed at any other time and if i had i would have not been raised bilingual or probably proud of my heritage neither could i have so easily gone to university and started my own business i do not romanticize the past but i do think it is full of rich stories that we need to know and i find nothing more fascinating than learning about the daily lives of people in any era much like we are fascinated with how other people live today it connects us to one another and trying out this technique was a wonderful way
to relate with other creatives who lived long ago and also liked experimenting with art do i will share some of my favorite books

about history in the description bar as well as details on how to make your own ciano type this was so much fun and i encourage you to try this technique out as the materials are affordable and can be used on fabric as well as paper de san do te una noche gena de pas e suenos ending my love sending my love you
zh: 昨天在小屋里度过了一个安静的夜晚，天很快就黑了，我的几朵娇嫩的花已经被清晨的霜冻住了，我试着每晚至少花半个小时读书，最近白天变得越来越短，我开始喜欢点燃蜡烛。我记得在爱尔兰读文学时，我读到人们过去如何使用牛脂蜡烛，它们是由动物脂肪制成的，闻起来很难闻，因此人们更喜欢石蜡和其他类型的蜡，并最终取代了它，我很感激可以让我的蜂蜡逐渐变细，我的家闻起来像
烤蜂蜜而不是动物脂肪 我发现每年这个时候使用较柔和的灯光有助于将我与这个季节联系起来，让我更多地意识到事物正在如何变化，它如何影响植物和动物，这是一年中最冷的半年的预兆，警告自然世界要在时间紧迫的情况下做好准备和抓紧时间
这里的三叶杨是最先落叶的，我认为它们的性格非常谨慎，就像我自己的一样，当事情看起来过于干燥或有一丝霜冻的时候，它们就开始减少叶子并进入休眠状态，其他树木很快也会效仿，小动物们忙着准备食物储备，我已经告别了这个地区的许多鸟儿，直到春天，我才不再嫉妒它们，因为在炎热无雨的夏季之后，我正在欢迎寒冷我的狗也是如此，每年这个时候他都喜欢在户外活动，因为他不会过热
所以本着季节变化的精神我

最近我想为我的家创造一些新的装饰，我读了很多关于过去的旧摄影技术的文章，自从今年我花了很多时间使用相机以来，我的兴趣达到了顶峰。制作蓝图的技术也被称为 canotypes，它起源于一百多年前，一位名叫安娜·阿德金斯 (anna adkins) 的女士因使用该技术制作藻类阴影图而闻名，该过程有着迷人的历史，并且在现代打印机流行之前仍在某些工作中使用如今，这项技术被对这一领域感兴趣的艺术家和摄影师保留了下来，他们的专业ciano类型无疑比我自己的业余尝试要好得多，但是尝试新事物并通过这些尝试是非常有趣的
时不时地重温过去更积极的方面，然后我在我的视频中收到评论，将我们今天的生活与过去的生活进行比较，经常浪漫化技术和工业化接管之前的时代，而在这些转变中肯定损失了很多，并且在此过程中发生了许多悲剧，我相信也有很多收获，这取决于你如何看待它，作为一个热爱历史并通过我自己的发现过程了解过去的人，我开始深深地重视生活，不仅在我的具体生活中

但在这个世纪，例如，我的母亲不是白人，她和我的父亲一直在努力让他们的婚姻在美国得到法律承认，直到60年代，我的存在在任何其他时候都不会得到保证，如果我有的话，我就不会在双语环境中长大，也不会为我的传统感到自豪，我也不会那么容易上大学并开始自己的事业，我不会浪漫化过去，但我确实认为它充满了我们需要知道的丰富故事，我发现没有什么比了解人们的日常生活更令人着迷的了任何时代的人们都像我们一样着迷于今天其他人的生活方式，它将我们彼此联系起来，尝试这种技术是一种很棒的方式
为了与其他生活在很久以前并且也喜欢尝试艺术的创意人士建立联系，我会分享一些我最喜欢的书吗
